#Bitcoin – What’s Next?

The Big Sunday Report: All We Need to Know

TA / LCA / Psychological Breakdown:

I remain bullish on the opportunity in front of us. If you turn time back, I was bullish in July at 60-64k, and guess who was bearish back then? All the bears that are bearish in these days, and the bears back then missed the entire run to 87k, and now we returned back to the exact place where it all started, and for some reason the bears celebrate the recent move, as if something would have changed for them. I  acknowledge that my recent long trade from $80K did not work as expected. That does not mean I become bearish on Bitcoin. As we speak the Fear & Greed Index has fallen to 10, reaching EXTREME FEAR. This is precisely when I become interested in accumulation again for the long term. Remember, there is a difference between trading which can be done at any price, and long term investing that should be done at potential market bottoms, spot positions that are built for the next 2-3 years, and we just returned to the area I am interested to buy for the long term, rather than focusing on trading. 

Bitcoin is massively oversold on the DAILY chart. The daily RSI reached approximately 19 which shows extreme over sold levels. The weekly RSI is around 43, which is slightly oversold on the Weekly. But what is interesting now on the chart is the triple bottom on the daily RSI that marked the local bottom precisely in the last months, as you can see in the chart. This would be one of the arguments to say , a local bottom is forming here, but there are more arguments to follow.

Lets have a look at the mining-cost for BTC, other words for its production, same as if you need to produce a chair, BTC has a production cost level as well. A production-cost estimate published earlier this month placed the cost around $61,200. For referrence, in June 2022, Glassnode estimated production costs around $17,200, while Bitcoin bottomed at 16,400 in the last bear market, nearby the production cost level. Historically, it turned out to be always very profitable to invest close to the Bitcoin production cost basis. 

Also, there was a very big liquidation cluster around $62K on the 6 month chart. Now I have a question about what happened on this Saturday: The person who sold Millions worth of Bitcoin, could have done so at higher volume moments, like during weekdays, he could have easily sold in smaller batches at 68k and the market would not have reacted much because of the higher volume. Why hit a thin market, on purpose during weekend with aggressive market selling, pushing Bitcoin from $68K toward $62K, almost 9% within hours? Exactly to the area where most of liquidations are located. I smell intention here. My interpretation is that the liquidation cluster was the target, it was wicked once for it so there might be another push for it and this is why I believe this area is the bottom.

My focus remains the same as in July this year. I am interested to expand my spot positions in the area of $60K–$64K region. Join Free Telegram: https://t.me/Therealdrprofit

THIS IS NOT FINANCIAL ADVICE, BUT EDUCATIONAL CONTENT ONLY.
